title: Who is God?
text: God is the One who made everything: the sky, the earth, the animals, and you. God has no beginning and no end, and He is always with us. We cannot see Him, but He sees us and loves us very much. The Bible says, God is love. We believe in one God in three Persons, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. We often call the first Person God the Father, because He is the loving Father of all. God is good, strong and kind. He listens when we pray, He takes care of us, and He wants us to be with Him forever. When we feel scared or alone, we can remember that God is near.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Did God make me? Who made me?
text: Yes! God made you. He made every person with love, and He made you exactly the way He wanted you to be. God knew you before you were born, and He has a special plan for your life. You are not an accident. That is why we say thank you to God for our eyes, our hands, our family and our friends. Your mom and dad helped bring you into the world, and God is the one who gives life to every person. Because God made us, every person is precious to Him, even people who look or sound different from us. We should treat everyone kindly, because God made them too. You are loved.

verse.text: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made

title: How old is the earth? Did God make the dinosaurs?
text: God made everything. The Bible begins with the words, In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth. Our Church teaches that God is the Creator of the sky, the sea, the land and every living thing. That is the most important thing for us to know and to be thankful for. How and when God made things, and how old the earth is, are questions that scientists study, and they are still learning new things. The Church does not ask children to worry about that. If you love dinosaurs, you can enjoy them and be amazed at how big and wonderful God's creation is. If you have more questions, you can ask Abouna or your teacher. It is good to be curious.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.

title: What is the Coptic Orthodox Church?
text: The Coptic Orthodox Church is the Christian church of Egypt. The word Coptic means Egyptian. Our church was founded by St. Mark the Apostle, who brought the good news of Jesus to Alexandria in Egypt, so it is one of the oldest churches in the world. The head of our church is the Pope of Alexandria, who follows St. Mark. We pray the Holy Liturgy, keep the seven sacraments, fast, love the saints and honor St. Mary. Today there are Coptic Orthodox churches in Egypt and all over the world, including right here. Many of our hymns and prayers are very old, and we keep them so that we can pray the way the first Christians did.

title: What does Orthodox mean?
text: Orthodox comes from two old Greek words. One means right or straight, and the other means worship or glory. So Orthodox means right faith and right worship. It means we hold on to the true faith about Jesus that the apostles handed down to the Church, and we worship God the way the Church has worshiped for a very long time. Coptic means Egyptian, as you learned. So Coptic Orthodox means the Orthodox Church of Egypt. Our church keeps the faith that was taught by St. Mark and the great fathers like St. Athanasius and St. Cyril. There are other Orthodox churches around the world too, and we are happy to be part of this family of faith.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Are there other churches? How are we different?
text: Yes, there are many Christian churches in the world, such as Catholic, Protestant (sometimes called Evangelical) and other Orthodox churches. All Christians love Jesus, believe in Him, and are baptized in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. We should respect everyone and be kind to all, because Jesus loves them. We are Coptic Orthodox. In our church we keep the traditions we received from the early Church: the seven sacraments, the Holy Liturgy, fasting, praying the Agpeya, using icons, asking the saints to pray for us, and honoring St. Mary the Theotokos. Churches can teach some things differently, and that is a big topic. When you are older, Abouna can explain more, and you can ask him any question you have.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Who are the twelve apostles?
text: An apostle is someone Jesus sent out to share the good news. Jesus chose twelve men to be close to Him, to learn from Him, and to be sent out to teach the world. They are Peter, Andrew, James the son of Zebedee, John, Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus (also called Jude), Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot. Judas later turned away, and the apostles chose Matthias to take his place. Later Jesus also called St. Paul to be an apostle, and the Church remembers many other apostles too. After the Holy Spirit came at Pentecost, the apostles traveled to many countries and told people about Jesus, and St. Mark brought the message to Egypt.

title: Who was Judas?
text: Judas Iscariot was one of the twelve apostles. He walked with Jesus, heard Him teach, and saw His miracles. But Judas let love of money grow in his heart. He agreed to tell the leaders where to find Jesus, and they paid him thirty pieces of silver. Later he felt very sorry for what he had done. The Bible tells us this sad story so that we can learn from it. We can choose to be loyal to Jesus and to love Him more than anything else. We should never choose money or anything else over Jesus and our friends. If we do make a mistake, we can say sorry to God and ask Him to forgive us. God is always ready to forgive when we come back to Him.

title: Why is Jesus called the Lamb of God?
text: When John the Baptist saw Jesus coming, he said, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world. A lamb is gentle and quiet, and it is also what the people of the Old Testament offered to God. At the first Passover in Egypt, a lamb was given and the families were kept safe. Jesus is the true Lamb. He gave Himself on the cross out of love, so that our sins could be forgiven and we could live with God. Jesus is also called the Good Shepherd, because He knows His sheep by name and takes care of them. We are His little lambs. That is why Lumi the lamb is a friendly helper in this app: a lamb reminds us of Jesus and of gentleness.

verse.text: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.

title: What is a prophet? Who are the prophets?
text: A prophet is a person God chose to speak His word to the people. God gave the prophets messages to tell the people to love Him, to do what is right, and to be ready for the Savior. Some prophets told about Jesus long before He was born. Elijah, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, Jonah and many others were prophets in the Old Testament. John the Baptist is the last and greatest prophet, because he pointed to Jesus and said, Behold the Lamb of God. Prophets were not always popular, and sometimes they were brave in hard times. We can learn from them to listen to God and to be brave in telling the truth. We read their words in the Bible and in the church readings.

verse.text: holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost

title: What is a miracle?
text: A miracle is something wonderful that only God can do. It goes beyond what people or nature can do on their own. In the Bible, Jesus did many miracles, because He is God and He loves people. He made the blind see, He healed the sick, He calmed the storm, He fed five thousand people with five loaves and two fish, and He raised Lazarus from the dead. These miracles showed His power and His kindness. Many saints also prayed, and God did miracles through them. Miracles still happen today when God answers prayers in ways we do not expect. God is never too small or too far away to help us. We can always pray to Him, and He will answer in the best way.

title: What is a saint? How does someone become a saint?
text: A saint is a holy person who loved God with all their heart and lived close to Him. Saints can be martyrs, monks, teachers, kings, mothers, fathers, or even children. In our church, we remember them and love them, and we ask them to pray for us. The Church does not have one big formal process to make someone a saint. Instead, the Church recognizes saints over time. People see how they lived, how they loved God, and how God worked through them, and the Church honors them. Their stories are read in the Synaxarium on their feast days. You do not need to be famous to be holy. Every one of us is called to become a saint by loving God and others, a little each day.

title: What is faith?
text: Faith means trusting God even when we cannot see Him. We cannot see the wind, but we see the leaves move and we know it is there. In the same way we cannot see God with our eyes, but we know He is with us because of what He has done. After the Resurrection, St. Thomas did not believe until he saw Jesus. Jesus said that those who believe without seeing are blessed. That means us! Faith is not just knowing about God. It is trusting Him when we are afraid, praying to Him, and doing what He asks. Our faith grows when we pray, read the Bible, go to church and take Holy Communion. Even a small faith can grow big.

verse.text: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.

title: What is Sunday School?
text: Sunday School is a place in the church where children come together to learn about Jesus, the Bible and our Coptic Orthodox faith. We hear Bible stories, learn about the saints and the feasts, memorize verses, sing hymns, play and make friends. Our teachers are servants. A servant is a person who gives their time to God and to us with love, and they learn together with us. Sunday School helps us to grow in our faith, to know how to pray, and to know the Church better. We also learn how to be kind and honest in our daily lives. Sunday School is a place where everyone is welcome, and where you can ask questions about God and the Church.

title: What are the four Gospels?
text: The word Gospel means good news. The good news is that Jesus came to save us. The four Gospels are the first four books of the New Testament: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John. Each one was written by a person led by the Holy Spirit, and each tells us the story of the life, the teaching, the miracles, the death and the Resurrection of Jesus. Matthew and John were apostles who followed Jesus. Mark and Luke were helpers of the apostles. Each Gospel tells the story in a slightly different way, like four friends describing the same wonderful day. In church, the Gospel is the most honored reading, and we stand while it is read. You can read them yourself in the Bible.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: What is the Temple and the Tabernacle?
text: In the Old Testament, God asked Moses to build a special tent called the Tabernacle, where the people could worship Him. They carried it with them in the desert. Later King Solomon built a beautiful Temple in Jerusalem, and the people came there to pray and bring offerings to God. The Temple was a holy place, because God's presence was with His people there. Our church building is like the Temple and the Tabernacle. It is the house of God, with an altar, incense, a haykal, and holy things. We behave with reverence in church because God is truly with us. Also, we ourselves are the temple of the Holy Spirit when we love God and live in a holy way.

verse.text: And let them make me a sanctuary; that I may dwell among them.

title: Who was King Herod?
text: Herod was a king who ruled Judea when Jesus was born. When the wise men came and asked where the new King of the Jews was, Herod became worried and jealous, because he wanted to stay king. He wanted to harm baby Jesus. But God protected Jesus. An angel told St. Joseph in a dream to take Mary and the child and go to Egypt. So the Holy Family traveled to Egypt, and that is how Egypt was blessed by Jesus' visit. When Herod was gone, the angel told Joseph it was safe, and they went home to Nazareth. This story teaches us that God takes care of us, and that no one can stop His plans. We are thankful that Jesus came to Egypt.

title: Who was Pontius Pilate?
text: Pontius Pilate was the Roman governor of Judea at the time of Jesus. The Jewish leaders brought Jesus to him, and Pilate had to decide what to do. Pilate asked Jesus questions, and he said that he found no fault in Him. But the crowd shouted loudly, and Pilate gave in because he was afraid of the people. He washed his hands in front of the crowd and then allowed Jesus to be crucified. Jesus did this willingly, out of love, to save us. This story teaches us to be brave and to do what is right, even when others around us are doing wrong. Pilate's name is also mentioned in the Creed that we pray in church.

title: What is the fruit of the Spirit?
text: When a tree is healthy, it grows good fruit. When the Holy Spirit lives in us, He makes good things grow in our hearts too. St. Paul wrote about them in his letter to the Galatians. The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control. Some of these are easy for us, and some take practice. We cannot grow them by ourselves. The Holy Spirit helps us when we pray, go to church, take Holy Communion and ask Him to help us. You can try one each day. For example, be patient with your brother, be kind to a new friend, or be gentle when you are upset. Over time, your heart will grow lovely fruit.

verse.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance

title: What is the Kingdom of God?
text: The Kingdom of God is where God is King, and where His love and His will are done. Jesus talked about it often. It is not like a kingdom of the world with soldiers and castles. It begins in our hearts when we love God and follow Jesus. It is also the happy life with God in heaven that will last forever. When we pray the Lord's Prayer and say, Thy kingdom come, we are asking that God's love, peace and goodness will grow here on earth too. Jesus said to put God first. We help the Kingdom of God grow when we are kind, tell the truth, forgive, share and pray. Heaven is a part of that Kingdom, where God lives with the angels and saints.

verse.text: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
